title: Ampanang language
description: Extinct Austronesian language of Kalimantan, Indonesia
extract: Ampanang is an extinct Austronesian language spoken at the village of Ampanang, at the Kahala river, modern-day East Kalimantan. It is closely related to Tunjung, forming the Mahakam languages. This language has extremely little documentation, and is only known from a 19-word vocabulary list on Beschrijving van de Onderafdeeling Koetei (1905). However, the 16th edition of the Ethnologue reported 30,000 speakers as of 1981.
